title: Microsoft Purview: auto-expanding archive limit rising from 1.5 TB to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing accurately reports the government-cloud rollout notice, eligible licensing and archive limits. Its PowerShell controls and restrictions are supported by Microsoft Learn, and it explicitly distinguishes the conflicting rollout dates and older limit text in Learn.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: title; front matter: clouds; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap describes previous expansion as limited to 1.5 TB, after which mailboxes would become inoperative.
claims.quote: Previously, auto-expanding archive mailbox expansion was supported only up to 1.5 TB, after which mailboxes would become inoperative.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans expansion beyond 1.5 TB for customers with eligible E5 licences.
claims.quote: This capability to expand archives beyond 1.5 TB will be available to customers with eligible E5 licenses.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Eligible Exchange Online archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can grow from the former 1.5 TB ceiling to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.
claims.quote: Eligible archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can automatically expand beyond the current 1.5 TB limit, up to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The increased ceiling arrives without administrator action for eligible mailboxes already using auto-expanding archiving, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: No action is required if eligible mailboxes already have auto-expanding archiving enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The increase is included with the listed eligible licences rather than separately metered.
claims.quote:
The increase applies to mailboxes assigned the following eligible licenses:
- Office 365 E5, A5, or G5
- Microsoft 365 E5, A5, or G5

claims.claim: No additional configuration is required for eligible mailboxes already using auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: No additional configuration is required for eligible mailboxes that already have auto-expanding archiving enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The increase introduces no per-GB consumption charge.
claims.quote: No per-GB consumption charge is introduced as part of this change.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing archive content is unchanged.
claims.quote: Existing archive content, retention configurations, policies, and holds are unchanged.

claims.claim: Existing retention configurations are unchanged.
claims.quote: Existing archive content, retention configurations, policies, and holds are unchanged.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing retention policies are unchanged.
claims.quote: Existing archive content, retention configurations, policies, and holds are unchanged.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing holds are unchanged.
claims.quote: Existing archive content, retention configurations, policies, and holds are unchanged.

claims.claim: No new administrator workflow is introduced.
claims.quote: No new administrator workflow, user experience, or user interface is introduced.

claims.claim: The notice describes no new user experience.
claims.quote: No new administrator workflow, user experience, or user interface is introduced.

claims.claim: No new user interface is introduced.
claims.quote: No new administrator workflow, user experience, or user interface is introduced.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: Mailboxes without eligible licences retain their existing 1.5 TB limit.
claims.quote: Mailboxes that do not have an eligible license will continue to be limited to 1.5 TB.

claims.claim: MC1521615 was published on 22 October 2026.
claims.quote: Published 2026-10-22; last updated 2026-10-22

claims.claim: The notice says General Availability rollout for GCC, GCC High and DoD begins in mid-November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026

claims.claim: The notice expects government-cloud rollout to complete by early December 2026.
claims.quote: is expected to complete by early December 2026.

claims.claim: The notice supplies no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: The Learn archive-page banner gives a rollout start of mid-October 2026.
claims.quote: Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October.

claims.claim: The Learn banner expects rollout completion by late October 2026.
claims.quote: Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October.

claims.claim: The Learn rollout banner does not name clouds.
claims.quote: Searched: auto expanding archiving enable admin center UI PowerShell Set-OrganizationConfig Enable-Mailbox no additional configuration 3 TB price; opened both cited Purview archive pages and read their complete banners, which give dates but name no clouds.

claims.claim: The body of Learn about auto-expanding archiving still describes a 1.5 TB maximum.
claims.quote: This archiving feature in Microsoft Purview (called auto-expanding archiving) provides up to 1.5 TB of additional storage in archive mailboxes.

claims.claim: Eligible archives gain headroom without a support request.
claims.quote: This enhancement helps organizations retain and manage larger volumes of archived email content without requiring manual archive expansion processes or support requests.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation, retention guidance and help desk materials.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, retention guidance, and help desk materials to reflect the new 3 TB limit.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends licence review and reviewing licensing and retention strategies for users with non-eligible archives.
claims.quote: Review license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility. ... Review licensing and retention strategies for users whose archive mailboxes are not eligible for the expanded capacity.

claims.claim: Learn continues to limit supported archive growth to no more than 1 GB per day.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported only for mailboxes used by individual users or for shared mailboxes with a growth rate that doesn't exceed 1 GB per day.

claims.claim: eDiscovery tools such as Content Search search the additional storage areas of auto-expanded archives.
claims.quote: When you use an eDiscovery tool, such as Content Search, the additional storage areas in an auto-expanded archive are also searched.

claims.claim: Mailbox holds also cover content in auto-expanded archives.
claims.quote: When you put a mailbox on hold by using methods such as Microsoft 365 retention, eDiscovery case holds, and Litigation Hold in Exchange Online, content located in an auto-expanded archive is also placed on hold.

claims.claim: No new permission or identity is described for the ceiling increase.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding" "3 TB" "price" "permissions"; opened both cited Purview archive pages and read MC1521615. The increase names eligible licences and no extra configuration, not a new identity or permission.

claims.claim: A global administrator can enable auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving, you must be a global administrator in your organization or a member of the Organization Management role group in your Exchange Online organization.

claims.claim: Membership in the Exchange Online Organization Management role group also permits enablement.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving, you must be a global administrator in your organization or a member of the Organization Management role group in your Exchange Online organization.

claims.claim: For specific users, membership in a role group including Mail Recipients suffices.
claims.quote: Alternately, to enable auto-expanding archiving for specific users, you must be a member of a role group that includes the Mail Recipients role.

claims.claim: After enablement, additional archive storage is added automatically.
claims.quote: When the archive mailbox gets close to its storage limit, additional storage space is automatically created

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators cannot adjust the storage quota or use these enablement controls to select the ceiling.
claims.quote: Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving cannot be turned off after enablement.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Per-user auto-expanding archiving cannot be turned off after enablement.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.claim: For E5 licences, Learn says to verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled.
claims.quote: For E5 licenses, verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled in the user's license settings.

claims.claim: Once an archive has an auto-expanded storage area, users cannot delete folders from the archive.
claims.quote: If an archive mailbox has at least one auto-expanded storage area, users can't delete a folder from the archive mailbox or from the auxiliary archive.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving prevents recovery or restoration of an inactive mailbox.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving prevents you from recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.

claims.claim: Office 365 E5, A5 and G5 are eligible licences.
claims.quote: Office 365 E5, A5, or G5

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5, A5 and G5 are eligible licences.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5, A5, or G5

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite FLW, EDU and GOV are eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite FLW, EDU, or GOV

claims.claim: Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 F5 Compliance is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 F5 Compliance

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 F5 Security + Compliance is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 F5 Security + Compliance

claims.claim: The combination of the eDiscovery & Audit, Insider Risk Management and Information Protection & Governance mini suites is eligible.
claims.quote: The combination of the eDiscovery & Audit, Insider Risk Management, and Information Protection & Governance mini suites

claims.claim: Qualifying offerings including Purview E5 capabilities, such as E7, also support the increase.
claims.quote: Qualifying offerings that include Microsoft Purview E5 capabilities, such as E7, also support the increase.

claims.claim: The cited Learn archive pages state no price for upgrading a user to an eligible licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding" "3 TB" "price" "permissions"; opened enable-autoexpanding-archiving and autoexpanding-archiving in full. Both list eligible licences and no per-GB charge, but neither gives a licence-upgrade price.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The user's archive mailbox must already be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports cloud-based archive mailboxes in Exchange hybrid deployments.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment for users who have an on-premises primary mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving is not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving isn't supported for on-premises mailboxes in any version of Exchange Server.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for organisation-wide auto-expanding archive enablement; Exchange Online PowerShell is required.
claims.quote: Searched: auto expanding archiving enable admin center UI PowerShell Set-OrganizationConfig Enable-Mailbox; opened enable-autoexpanding-archiving, which explicitly prohibits enabling through Exchange admin center or Purview portal and requires Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for per-user auto-expanding archive enablement; Exchange Online PowerShell is required.
claims.quote: Searched: auto expanding archiving enable admin center UI PowerShell Set-OrganizationConfig Enable-Mailbox; opened enable-autoexpanding-archiving, which explicitly prohibits enabling through Exchange admin center or Purview portal and requires Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote:
To enable auto-expanding archiving for your entire organization, run the following command:
Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables auto-expanding archiving for a specific user, subject to the row's prerequisites.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user, run the following command. ... Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: The per-user command requires both primary and archive mailboxes to be cloud-based.
claims.quote: If a user's primary and archive mailboxes are both cloud-based, then you can use the Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command to enable auto-expanding archiving for that specific user.

claims.claim: For an on-premises primary mailbox with a cloud archive, Learn requires organisation-wide Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive instead of per-user Enable-Mailbox.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment, you have to run the Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive command in Exchange Online PowerShell to enable auto-expanding archiving for the entire organization.

claims.claim: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks organisation-wide enablement.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks per-user enablement.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for a specific user, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement does not set the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on individual user mailboxes to True.
claims.quote: Running the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to enable auto-expanding archiving for your organization doesn't change the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on user mailboxes to True.

claims.claim: Per-user enablement adds 10 GB to the archive quota when the mailbox is on hold or assigned a retention policy.
claims.quote: When you enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user and the user's mailbox in on hold or assigned to a retention policy ... The storage quota for the user's primary archive mailbox is increased by 10 GB (from 100 GB to 110 GB).

claims.claim: The pages for this change do not state what happens to an archive already above 1.5 TB if its eligible licence is removed.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving 3 TB eligible license removed downgrade 1.5 TB; opened both cited Purview archive pages and read MC1521615. They state eligible and other-licence ceilings but do not describe removing eligibility after growth above 1.5 TB.

controlChecks.governs: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation
